goal: Review the captureState mutex pattern in internal/runner/runner.go and identify which fields can safely move to sync/atomic without breaking heartbeat/timeout semantics. Cite file:line evidence and call out fields that must stay under the mutex.
background: Scope: internal/runner/runner.go ONLY. Do not review or recommend changes to other files.
Target pattern: the captureState struct and its mutex usage in this file.

Required prior reading: runs/2026-05-21-4704/report.md contains a consensus comparison of sync/atomic vs sync.Mutex for hot counters and atomic.Pointer[time.Time] for last-output timestamps. Read it BEFORE reviewing so the recommendations align with that consensus.

Focus: classify each mutex-protected field in captureState into one of: (a) safe to move to sync/atomic with a specific atomic type and migration sketch; (b) safe with caveats — explain the caveat (e.g. memory-ordering constraint, paired-read invariant, timestamp publication); (c) must stay under sync.Mutex — explain why (e.g. multi-field invariant, byte-slice append, compound state transition).

Heartbeat/timeout semantics: the runner emits periodic heartbeats and enforces wall-clock + idle timeouts based on the captured state. Any atomic conversion must preserve: (1) heartbeat lines report consistent counters and last-output timestamps, (2) the idle-timeout check sees a monotonic or correctly-published timestamp, (3) wall-clock budget enforcement is not weakened, (4) no torn reads of paired fields (e.g. byte counts read together with truncation flags).

Evidence standard: every finding must cite internal/runner/runner.go:<line> for the field, the lock site, and the read site. When recommending atomic.Pointer[time.Time] or atomic.Int64, reference the consensus from the prior report by section/topic.
Out of scope: rewriting the file, proposing patches, changing the public API, adding new fields, modifying tests, or reviewing any file other than internal/runner/runner.go.

facet.focus: Classify each captureState field as atomic-safe, atomic-with-caveats, or mutex-only, with respect to heartbeat/timeout semantics. Produce a per-field verdict table with file:line evidence.
include: per-field verdict: atomic-safe / atomic-with-caveats / mutex-only, with the specific atomic type when applicable
concrete migration sketch (5-15 lines) for each atomic-safe field
named invariants that would break if a field moved out of the mutex (multi-field atomicity, paired reads, compound transitions)
race-detector and memory-ordering risks specific to heartbeat/timeout call sites
torn-read or publication risks for time.Time fields and their interaction with idle-timeout checks
exclude: rewrites or patches to internal/runner/runner.go (review only, not implementation)
recommendations that affect any file other than internal/runner/runner.go
style-only preferences without a correctness or performance argument
speculation without file:line evidence from internal/runner/runner.go
generic Go concurrency advice not tied to a specific field in captureState
